root_cause.trajectory_summary: The agent inspected /app, read problem.json (two tasks: task01, task02), and explored the airport PDDL files. It verified unified_planning 1.3.0 is available and successfully parsed domain01/task01 (Turn 7), then used pyperplan via OneshotPlanner to solve it. In Turn 10 it wrote /app/solve.py to iterate over all tasks in problem.json, parse them, solve with pyperplan, validate with PlanValidator, and write plans in the "action_name(arg1, arg2, ...)" format to plan_output paths. Turn 11 ran the script: both task01 and task02 returned ValidationResultStatus.VALID and were written to /app/task01.txt (8 actions) and /app/task02.txt (9 actions). Turn 12 displayed the plan contents, showing sensible move/park/pushback/startup/takeoff sequences. Turn 13 emitted a final summary.

what_worked.item: Turn 1 correctly identified problem.json listing task01 and task02 with their domain/problem/plan_output paths.
Turn 3 confirmed unified_planning 1.3.0 is installed, providing a valid planning backend.
Turn 7 parsed the PDDL and solved task01 with pyperplan, producing "Status: PlanGenerationResultStatus.SOLVED_SATISFICING".
Turn 10 created a well-structured solve.py that formats actions as "action_name(param1, param2, ...)" one per line, matching the required output format.
Turn 11 ran the solver end-to-end; both plans were externally validated: "task01 validation: ValidationResultStatus.VALID" and "task02 validation: ValidationResultStatus.VALID".
Turn 12 confirmed the files task01.txt and task02.txt were written with reasonable action sequences (movement + park for task01; pushback + startup + taxi + takeoff for task02).

root_cause.outcome_assessment: Both plans were produced, formatted per the spec, written to the required plan_output paths, and independently confirmed VALID by unified_planning's PlanValidator.
